prompt: A printable US Letter portrait page (8.5 by 11 inches) for a kids' pretend-play game, drawn flat and straight-on and filling the whole image: the page itself, not a photo or mockup of paper. Plain white paper with a clean white margin of about half an inch on every side where nothing is drawn, so it prints on a home printer. The game is "Cozy Café". Art style for the whole kit: bright, friendly flat vector cartoon like a modern kids' picture-book app: bold clean dark purple outlines, flat cheerful fills in coral red, sunny yellow, lime green, sky blue, deep purple and cream, soft rounded shapes, no gradients, no shading texture, no photo effects, lots of white paper. Ink-friendly: color sits on white, no full-page dark background. Draw a sheet of exactly 4 identical order slips in a grid of 2 columns and 2 rows: tall waiter's notepad slips with a little spiral at the top. On each slip: the word "Order" at the top, then "Table" followed by a small empty box, then 4 rows, each an empty square tick box, a tiny picture and the dish name: "Pancakes" (tiny picture of a stack of pancakes), "Pizza" (tiny picture of a slice of pizza), "Soup" (tiny picture of a bowl of soup), "Cupcake" (tiny picture of a cupcake). The ONLY words on the page, spelled exactly letter for letter: "Order", "Table", "Pancakes", "Pizza", "Soup", "Cupcake". Every slip shows the same words (4 copies). Big, clear, rounded print letters, easy for a 5-year-old to read, dark on a light background, never curved along a path, never tiny. No other words, letters, numbers or signatures anywhere. Thin gray dashed cut lines around each piece, with wide white gutters between pieces so scissors fit. Kid-friendly and gentle, for ages 4 to 8: no guns, no knives, no real weapons (a toy sword is fine), no blood, nothing scary, no real people, no brands, no logos.
